:::{#exm-random-experiment}
#### Picking a car model from the Auto data

The Auto data record the number of engine cylinders and the fuel economy
(miles per gallon) of
`{r} nrow(read.csv("data/auto.csv"))` car models
sold between 1970 and 1982.
They come from the StatLib library at Carnegie Mellon University
and ship with the book *An Introduction to Statistical Learning*
and the R package [`ISLR2`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ISLR2)
(`ISLR2::Auto`).
This site has a copy at [`data/auto.csv`](data/auto.csv).

Pick one car model from the data without looking, and record its number of cylinders.
Which model comes up is not determined in advance,
so this procedure is a random experiment.
Its possible outcomes are the cylinder counts that occur in the data:

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# read the local copy of the Auto data (one row per car model):
auto <- read.csv("data/auto.csv")

# the possible outcomes are the distinct cylinder counts in the data:
sort(unique(auto$cylinders))
```
:::
